options.text: Consultants and vendors with system access

questions.text: Which company resources does this policy cover?
questions.template: It covers the following Company resources: {1.2}, wherever they are used — in the office, at home or while travelling.

questions.text: Can employees use their personal devices for work (BYOD)?
questions.example: Yes — phones and laptops, with approval and required security settings
questions.template: Use of personal devices for work: {1.3}.

options.wording: Personal devices may not be used for work; only Company-provided devices are permitted.

options.text: Yes — personal phones for email and chat only
options.wording: Personal phones may be used for work email and chat only.

options.text: Yes — phones and laptops, with approval and required security settings
options.wording: Personal phones and laptops may be used for work with prior approval and only with the required security settings in place.
Personal devices may be used for work without restriction.

questions.text: What must personal devices have before being used for work?
questions.template: Personal devices used for work must have: {1.4}.

options.text: Screen lock with PIN, password or biometrics
Company may remotely wipe company data

questions.text: Does your organization monitor the use of company systems?
questions.help: Employees must be told clearly that they have no expectation of privacy on company systems.
questions.template: Employees have no expectation of privacy when using Company systems. {2.1}.

options.wording: Employees have no expectation of privacy when using Company systems. The Company actively monitors the use of its systems.

options.text: Yes — we reserve the right but monitor only when needed (e.g., investigations)
options.wording: Employees have no expectation of privacy when using Company systems. The Company reserves the right to monitor the use of its systems and does so when needed, for example during investigations.
The Company does not monitor the use of its systems.

questions.text: What may be monitored?
questions.example: Email; Internet browsing; Login and access activity
questions.template: The Company may monitor and log: {2.2}.

options.text: Chat and collaboration tools (e.g., Teams, Slack)
File uploads, downloads and USB use

questions.text: Who can access monitoring records?
questions.example: IT / Information Security team; Human Resources (for investigations)
questions.template: Monitoring records may only be accessed by {2.3}.

options.text: External auditors or authorities when legally required

questions.text: How long are monitoring logs kept?

options.wording: Monitoring logs are retained for 90 days.
Monitoring logs are retained for six months.
Monitoring logs are retained for one year.

options.text: 3 years or more / as required by law
options.wording: Monitoring logs are retained for three years or longer where required by law.
Monitoring logs are retained for {fill}.

questions.text: Is personal use of company systems allowed?
questions.example: Limited, reasonable use during breaks or outside working hours
questions.template: Company systems are provided for business purposes. Personal use is {3.1}, provided it does not interfere with work, consume excessive resources or create risk.

options.wording: Company systems are provided for business purposes only; personal use is not allowed.

options.text: Limited, reasonable use during breaks or outside working hours
options.wording: Company systems are provided for business purposes. Limited, reasonable personal use is allowed during breaks or outside working hours, provided it does not interfere with work, consume excessive resources or create risk.

options.text: Limited, reasonable use at any time if it does not affect work
options.wording: Company systems are provided for business purposes. Limited, reasonable personal use is allowed at any time, provided it does not affect work, consume excessive resources or create risk.

questions.text: Which personal activities are acceptable?
questions.example: Personal email (webmail); Online banking and bill payments; News and general browsing

options.text: Storing personal files on company devices

questions.text: Is personal content on company devices treated as private?
questions.example: No — anything on company systems may be accessed by the Company

options.text: No — anything on company systems may be accessed by the Company
options.wording: Employees should have no expectation of privacy for personal content on Company systems; anything stored on Company systems may be accessed by the Company.

options.text: Personal folders are respected except during investigations
options.wording: Personal folders on Company systems are respected, except during investigations.

questions.text: Which activities are prohibited? (all are recommended)

options.text: Accessing, storing or sharing illegal, offensive, sexually explicit or discriminatory content
Installing unapproved software or browser extensions
Using pirated software, music or video
Bypassing security controls (personal VPNs, proxies, disabling antivirus)
Sharing accounts or using someone else's account
Accessing systems or data without authorization
Connecting unauthorized devices to the network (personal routers, unknown USBs)
Running a personal business or side job
Large downloads or streaming that slow the network

options.note: Opens text box: Additional prohibited activity

questions.text: How is software installed on company devices?

options.wording: Only the IT team may install software on Company devices.

options.text: Employees choose from an approved self-service catalog
options.wording: Employees may install software only from the Company's approved self-service catalogue.

options.text: Employees may install with manager approval
options.wording: Employees may install software only with their manager's approval.

questions.text: Minimum password length
questions.template: Passwords must be at least {5.1} long.

options.wording: Passwords must be at least 8 characters long.
Passwords must be at least 12 characters long.
Passwords must be at least 14 characters long.

options.text: As enforced by our IT systems
options.wording: Passwords must meet the length requirements enforced by the Company's IT systems.

questions.text: How often must passwords be changed?
questions.example: Only when compromise is suspected (current best practice)

options.wording: Passwords must be changed every 90 days.
Passwords must be changed every 180 days.

options.text: Only when compromise is suspected (current best practice)
options.wording: Passwords must be changed whenever a compromise is suspected.
Passwords must be changed {fill}.

questions.text: Where is multi-factor authentication (MFA) required?
questions.example: Email and office suite; VPN / remote access; Administrator accounts

questions.text: Is a password manager approved?

options.wording: Work passwords must be stored in the Company-approved password manager, {fill}.
Password managers must not be used for work passwords.
The Company has not yet approved a standard password manager.

questions.text: Screens must lock automatically after how long?
questions.template: Employees must lock their screen when leaving their device; screens lock automatically after {5.5} of inactivity.

options.wording: Employees must lock their screen when leaving their device; screens lock automatically after 5 minutes of inactivity.
Employees must lock their screen when leaving their device; screens lock automatically after 10 minutes of inactivity.
Employees must lock their screen when leaving their device; screens lock automatically after 15 minutes of inactivity.
Employees must lock their screen when leaving their device; screens lock automatically after {fill} of inactivity.

questions.text: Credential rules employees must follow (all recommended)

options.text: Never share passwords with anyone, including IT
Never reuse work passwords on other sites
Never write passwords down or store them in plain text
Report any suspected password compromise immediately

questions.text: What data classification levels do you use?

options.wording: Company information is classified as Public, Internal, Confidential or Restricted.
Company information is classified as Public, Internal or Confidential.
Company information is classified according to the Company's own scheme: {fill}.

options.text: None yet — use the recommended levels
options.wording: Company information is classified as Public, Internal, Confidential or Restricted.

questions.template: Company data may only be stored in: {6.2}.

USB drives and other removable media may be used freely.

questions.text: Rules for sending confidential data outside the company

options.text: Must be encrypted or password protected
Only through approved secure file-sharing tools
An NDA or contract must be in place

questions.text: Rules for handling personal data (customers and employees)
questions.template: When handling personal data, employees must: {6.5}.

options.text: Access only what your job requires

questions.text: Clean desk and printing rules
What is your position on generative AI tools (chatbots, writing and coding assistants)?
questions.help: Unapproved AI tools are one of the most common sources of data leaks today.

options.wording: The use of generative AI tools for work is prohibited.
Only Company-approved generative AI tools may be used for work.

options.text: Allowed — any tool, for public information only
options.wording: Any generative AI tool may be used for work, but only with public information.
Until the Company decides its position on generative AI, only approved tools may be used and no confidential information may be entered into any AI tool.

questions.template: Approved AI tools: {7.2}. Personal or free accounts must not be used for work.

options.note: Opens text box: Other restricted data

options.text: A person must review output before it is used
Facts must be verified before relying on them
Disclose AI use in external-facing content
AI must not be used alone for decisions about people (hiring, performance)

options.text: Only IT-approved tools may be used

options.text: Allowed via a company-managed business account

options.wording: Automatically forwarding work email to personal accounts is prohibited.

questions.text: Social media rules
questions.template: On social media, employees must follow these rules: {8.4}.

options.text: Only authorized staff may speak on behalf of the Company
Personal opinions must not appear to be the Company's
Do not post photos of screens, documents or restricted areas
Be respectful — no harassment of colleagues or customers
Disclose your employment when discussing Company products

questions.text: Who is authorized to speak publicly for the Company?
questions.template: Only {8.5} may make public statements on behalf of the Company.

questions.text: Email communication rules

options.text: Be cautious with unexpected links and attachments

questions.text: What must employees report? (all recommended)

options.text: Lost or stolen devices or access cards
Data sent to the wrong person

questions.text: How should incidents be reported?
questions.example: Email — security@acme.com; 'Report phishing' button in email

questions.text: How quickly must incidents be reported?

options.wording: Incidents must be reported immediately, and in any case within one hour.
Incidents must be reported on the same working day.
Incidents must be reported within 24 hours.

questions.text: Include a non-retaliation statement?

options.text: Yes — good-faith reports will never be punished
options.wording: Reports made in good faith will never lead to punishment.

questions.text: Is remote working permitted?

options.wording: Remote working is not permitted.
Employees may work in a hybrid arrangement, partly from the office and partly remotely.
Employees may work fully remotely.
Remote working is allowed case by case, with prior approval.

questions.text: Network rules when working remotely
questions.example: Company VPN must be used; Public Wi-Fi only with VPN; Home Wi-Fi must be password protected

options.text: Home Wi-Fi must be password protected

questions.text: Device rules outside the office (all recommended)

options.text: Do not let family members or others use work devices
Lock the screen whenever stepping away
Use a privacy screen in public places
Never leave devices unattended in cars or public places
Keep the operating system and apps updated

questions.text: Can employees work from another country?

options.wording: Working from abroad is not permitted without prior written approval.

options.wording: The Company owns all work created during employment or using Company resources.

questions.text: When must company assets be returned?
questions.example: On the last working day; Upon Company request

questions.text: What must be returned?

options.text: All Company data — no copies may be kept

questions.text: When is system access removed for leavers?

options.wording: System access is removed on the employee's last working day.

options.text: Immediately on notice for sensitive roles, otherwise last working day
options.wording: System access is removed immediately on notice for sensitive roles, and on the last working day for everyone else.
System access is removed within 24 hours of leaving.

questions.text: Company data on personal devices when leaving
questions.example: Must be deleted and confirmed in writing
questions.template: On leaving, Company data on personal devices {12.4}.

options.text: Must be deleted and confirmed in writing
options.wording: On leaving, Company data on personal devices must be deleted and the deletion confirmed in writing.

options.text: The Company will remotely wipe Company data
options.wording: On leaving, the Company will remotely wipe Company data from personal devices.

questions.text: What happens if assets are not returned?

If Company assets are not returned, their cost may be deducted from the final settlement (as permitted by law) and legal action may be taken.
